Mar'dy had sat in front of the Keemana Vial. There it was. Ready to kill him if he so wished. He was filled with nothing but despair.

The news from Kureta was horrible, the way the messenger described the Lethe creatures haunted his dreams now. Like if it was illness. The messenger was in a horrible state, vomiting, shaking, crying and screaming all night. When they found him in the morning, he was covered in blood, his own dagger in his hand. As if out of some desperation he reverted to cutting patterns into his own skin. They were all fear wards, patterns meant to mark dangerous locations, carved hundreds of times into his own flesh. Sa'vak had taken to ending the misery of the poor wreck himself.

All around him things were starting to crumble, the Thorac started to argue. Some said it was the end of times, some said it was too late. The Saen seemed hardy, but their councils were secretive. There was no where for Mar'dy to turn. He grabbed the vial and ran off deep into the forest. He ran until his feet hurt then stopped, there was something shiny in the ground.

He began to dig in the soft soil, eventually finding the wreck of an old sentinel. These things were meant for order. These things were meant to end suffering but as this offered to Gaea, Gaea rejected it. Instead we fought to our bloody death in order to suffer more? Sickly thoughts entered his mind. Fear and Death. He remembered his first gladiator fight, the first Lot'dy he killed. It was actually an old Steward dissident sent to die. He couldn't remember what the old Steward kept repeating as he stabbed him over and over.

There in the dark forest, the night began to fall and wild animals called their nocturnal cries. What did that Steward say? He said something. Mar'dy fell asleep rocking back and forth on his ground.

He was back in the arena. It was meant to be an easy fight to introduce new gladiators. Three of them were sent to kill three old Lot'dy. The first blood, meant to harden you. Mar'dy stabbed the old Lot'dy Steward in the foot. It barely gashed him. His arm feel weak as he struck at him. Even with his resolve to kill or be killed he couldn't find the strength. As if someone was holding him back. He stabbed harder and harder, the old Lot'dy murmuring to himself as Mar'dy struck him. Tears began to leave Mar'dy eyes. "What are you saying!" He shouted at him. He stabbed him harder and harder. "What are you saying!" The old Lot'dy turned back at him suddenly, a grin across his face, a fresh face, fiery eyes. Mar'dy fell back and blackness surrounded him. The old voice started to speak, as if chanting. "I don't fear death. Death is freedom. Death is freedom. Death is freedom."

Mar'dy awoke in the night. His arms stopped shaking. The Lethe were freeing the people of Kureta from their lives. This is a good thing. He started his walk back to the camp. Death is good thing.

He stood upon the deck of a ship, a great battle ebbed around him. On the opposite side of the ship, stood Mar'dy. Surrounded by Naga and Ha'lot'dy, a hopeless position. Mar'dy reached for something at his neck, a vial. What was it that he carried? The ship tilted, and Sa'vak never saw what happened next. But that vial, Mar'dy had reached for it, and he had lived. Perhaps it was something magical? But how, surely it must be the reason that he survived?

Sa'vak continued to watch Mar'dy as he rocked himself to sleep upon the jungle floor. He knew that desperation, the past haunted his steps too. It was the reason he had slept so little, except there was something peaceful about this forest, like a blanket of calm, wrapping him up and protecting him, the dreams came few and far in between lately. But Mar'dy, something was preying upon his mind? Something would need to be done, for Sa'vak couldn't fail another master.
